segments.text: The core invite flow is ready. Safari and expired SSO certificates are the two remaining checks.
I can finish Safari today; Sam owns certificate rotation.
Rotation works on staging. We still need the rollback rehearsal.
Release to five pilot tenants only after both checks pass. Riya, collect the QA sign-off. I will own the final rollout checklist.
Decision: Gate the workspace pilot on Safari and SSO rollback checks. Reason: Both checks protect the primary sign-in path. Considered: Release to every tenant; Skip the rollback rehearsal.
Decision: Start the workspace pilot with five tenants. Reason: A small reversible cohort limits the blast radius.
Final action owners and calendar dates replace the relative dates mentioned earlier. These are the agreed follow-ups.
Action: Approve the tenant-workspace rollout checklist. Owner: Archit Gupta. Due: 2026-11-15. Status: pending.
Action: Finish Safari invite and SSO smoke tests. Owner: Vedant Moghe. Due: 2026-11-15. Status: in progress.
Action: Collect QA sign-off for the five-tenant pilot. Owner: Riya. Due: 2026-11-16. Status: pending.
Action: Rehearse certificate rotation and rollback. Owner: Sam. Due: 2026-11-16. Status: pending.
Risk to watch: An untested certificate rollback could interrupt pilot sign-ins. Severity: High.
Open question: Who is the backup approver if the release owner is unavailable?
These notes are a synthetic software-team scenario for the demo. No customer account, external ticket or email was created.

answers.question: Why PostgreSQL?
answers.answer: The team chose PostgreSQL for atomic ledger writes, unique constraints and reliable invoice reconciliation.

answers.question: What’s blocking the release?
answers.answer: Safari smoke tests, certificate rollback and QA sign-off are the remaining gates for the five-tenant pilot.

answers.question: Why defer Redis?
answers.answer: The metadata index met the target in a synthetic benchmark, so the team deferred Redis and its invalidation complexity.
